title: Search in a Rotated Array

concept.title: One half is always sorted
body: A sorted array of different numbers was rotated: `4 5 6 7 0 1 2`. If you cut it in the middle, at least one half is still sorted. You can tell which one by comparing `a[lo]` with `a[mid]`: if `a[lo] <= a[mid]`, the left half is sorted.

body.code:
if a[lo] <= a[mid]:              # left half is sorted
    if a[lo] <= x < a[mid]: hi = mid - 1
    else: lo = mid + 1
else:                            # right half is sorted
    if a[mid] < x <= a[hi]: lo = mid + 1
    else: hi = mid - 1

body: In the sorted half you can check with two comparisons whether `x` can be inside it. If yes, search there; if no, search the other half. Each step still halves the range.

statement: A sorted array of `n` different integers was rotated at an unknown place (for example `0 1 2 4 5 6 7` can become `4 5 6 7 0 1 2`). Given the rotated array and a number `x`, print the index of `x` (counting from 0), or -1 if it is not in the array.
inputFormat: The second line has the rotated array.
hints: After cutting at `mid`, one of the two halves is sorted.
The left half is sorted when `a[lo] <= a[mid]`.
Test whether `x` lies between the ends of the sorted half; if yes go there, otherwise go to the other half.
